title: Mystery Window / Process Diagnosis: why did this console appear?
desc: Diagnose any unexpected window or process that appeared without user action. Covers Claude console pop-up, scheduled task consoles, pending_prompts delivery, WkAutoQuant hourly cycle, Eye-spawned subprocesses. Pattern: eye tick -> windows list -> screenshot -> read.
steps: WHEN TO USE: any time a console, Claude session, or process appeared without you starting it. Also when you see an active window with an unfamiliar title and want to know what is running.

STEP 1 -- eye tick: run wkappbot eye tick. Shows all running Claude sessions with task name, ctx%, and last thought lines. If the mystery window has a recognizable task name (e.g. 'hourly cycle', 'Stage 4'), it is a scheduled automation -- not caused by anything you did.

STEP 2 -- list windows: run wkappbot windows "*wkchat*;*claude*;*Claude Code*" --all. Lists every terminal tab with hwnd, title, process. Look for bare titles like 'claude' (no project prefix) or unfamiliar descriptions.
STEP 3 -- screenshot: run wkappbot a11y screenshot "{hwnd:0xXXXX,...}". Copy the PNG path from SAVED:... line, then use Read tool to view it.

STEP 4 -- read the screenshot: look for (A) stage labels like 'Stage 4c' or 'hourly cycle' -> scheduled automation. (B) repo/file paths in output -> which project. (C) flags like --permission-mode bypassPermissions -> unattended claude -p run. (D) Korean task summaries -> WkAutoQuant cycle.

COMMON ORIGINS -- Claude console pop-up: (A) WkAutoQuant hourly cycle: claude -p --permission-mode bypassPermissions on cron, new tab every hour. (B) pending_prompts delivery: Eye injected a pending file into an existing session -- no new window. (C) wkappbot newchat: explicit handoff launched a tab. (D) Eye watchdog restart: VBS killed Eye after 2min, restarted with fresh wkchat. (E) EnsureClaudeGuideSetup: first-run CLAUDE.md append, stderr only, no window.

BROADER PATTERN -- any mystery process: (1) wkappbot windows <title-glob>. (2) wkappbot a11y inspect {hwnd:...} for PID and cmd. (3) wkappbot windows --process <name> --cmd <substr>. (4) schtasks /query /fo LIST for scheduled tasks. (5) Eye log for restart events.
